alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic deterioration
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year when initiating or transitioning to DTG. Patient transitioned to DTG 18 months ago and has gained 17 kg (65 to 82 kg), BMI rising from 25.6 to 32.4. New acanthosis nigricans confirms developing insulin resistance. Fasting glucose increased from 92 to 118 mg/dL and HbA1c is 6.1% (pre-diabetic). BP rose from 118/74 to 138/88. DTG is associated with weight gain, supporting drug attribution. However, family history of Type 2 Diabetes also contributes to metabolic risk. Lipid abnormalities (LDL 148, triglycerides 212) further compound cardiovascular risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3 months as per DTG monitoring algorithm. Counsel on diet and exercise. Consider metformin if progression continues.

alerts.title: Missing DTG glucose monitoring per guideline schedule
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after DTG initiation. Patient has been on DTG for 18 months with no documented prior glucose monitoring in the provided records. Today's labs show impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%), indicating the monitoring schedule was not followed. The clinician's plan today is blank, with no orders for follow-up glucose monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Order fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3 months. Document a metabolic monitoring plan addressing weight, BP, and glycemic trends.
